content.content:
1	# obsd
2	
3	Minimal, dependency-free backend skeleton for **metrics ingestion, alerting and
4	SLO tracking**. Python 3.10+, standard library only, offline, deterministic
5	(every time-dependent entry point takes an injected `now_ms`).
6	
7	The lane goal is a metrics collection, alerting and SLO backend that grows
8	towards time-series writes and downsampling, label indexing and a query subset,
9	aggregation and sliding windows, alert rules with silencing and inhibition,
10	notification routing and dedup, SLO and error-budget math, retention and
11	compaction, multi-tenant quota, access control and audit, and consistent reads
12	under high availability. This seed implements the first, smallest *real* slice of
13	each of those areas.
14	
15	## Run
16	
17	```bash
18	# HTTP API (data dir flag is global and comes BEFORE the subcommand)
19	python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
20	
21	# test suite
22	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	Both commands are run offline with the system interpreter; no third-party
26	package is imported anywhere.
27	
28	## CLI
29	
30	`python3 -m obsd [--data-dir ./obsd_data] <command> ...` prints exactly one line
31	of JSON on stdout. On error it prints one line of JSON (`{"error":"..."}`) on
32	stderr and exits non-zero.
33	
34	| Command | Example |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `serve` | `python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` |
37	| `quota-set` | `python3 -m obsd quota-set --tenant acme --max-series 1000 --max-points 1000000` |
38	| `quota-get` | `python3 -m obsd quota-get --tenant acme` |
39	| `write` | `python3 -m obsd write --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --label host=a --sample 1000:12.5 --now-ms 2000` |
40	| `query` | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --agg avg` |
41	| `query` (grouped) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --agg avg --group-by '["host"]'` |
42	| `query` (matchers) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --matchers '[{"key":"host","op":"=~","value":"api-.*"}]'` |
43	| `query` (sliding window) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --window-ms 5000 --agg avg` |
44	| `rule-add` | `python3 -m obsd rule-add --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --comparator "<" --threshold 10 --window-ms 60000 --for-ms 30000 --agg avg --severity warning` |
45	| `eval` | `python3 -m obsd eval --now-ms 68000` |
46	| `alerts` | `python3 -m obsd alerts --tenant acme --state firing` |
47	| `silence-add` | `python3 -m obsd silence-add --tenant acme --starts-ms 0 --ends-ms 90000 --reason maintenance` |
48	| `slo set` | `python3 -m obsd slo set --tenant acme --name availability --metric latency_ms --good-comparator ">=" --threshold 1 --target-ratio 0.9 --window-ms 60000` |
49	| `slo status` | `python3 -m obsd slo status --name availability --now-ms 60000` |
50	
51	## HTTP API
52	
53	Errors are always JSON: `{"error":"..."}` with status 400 (bad request),
54	404 (unknown resource) or 409 (write conflict or quota exceeded).
55	
56	| Method | Path | Request | Response |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| GET | `/healthz` | – | `200 {"ok":true}` |
59	| POST | `/v1/series` | `{"tenant","metric","labels","samples":[[ts,value],...]}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"series_id":"..."}`, `409` on conflicting timestamp or quota exceeded |
60	| GET | `/v1/query` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&step=&agg=&group_by=&window=&matchers=` (group_by and matchers are JSON arrays; matchers holds `{"key","op","value"}` objects) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}` |
61	| POST | `/v1/quotas` | `{"tenant","max_series":n\|null,"max_points":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/limits give `400` and leave config untouched |
62	| GET | `/v1/quotas` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports `null` limits and real usage) |
63	| POST | `/v1/rules` | rule object | `201` stored rule |
64	| GET | `/v1/rules` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"rules":[...]}` |
65	| POST | `/v1/evaluate` | `{"now_ms":n}` | `200 {"firing":[...],"silenced":[...],"inhibited":[...],"resolved":[...]}` |
66	| GET | `/v1/alerts` | `?tenant=&state=` | `200 {"alerts":[...]}` |
67	| POST | `/v1/silences` | `{"tenant","labels","starts_ms","ends_ms","reason"}` | `201` stored silence |
68	| POST | `/v1/inhibitions` | `{"source_severity","target_severity","same_labels"}` | `201` stored inhibition |
69	| POST | `/v1/slos` | `{"tenant","name","metric","labels","good_comparator","threshold","target_ratio","window_ms"}` | `201` stored SLO |
70	| GET | `/v1/slos/status` | `?tenant=&name=&now_ms=` | `200` SLO status object |
71	| GET | `/v1/stats` | – | `200 {"store":{...},"alerts":n}` |
72	
73	## Data model
74	
75	A series identity is `(tenant, metric, sorted(label pairs))`. The canonical
76	identity string joins the tenant, the metric and every `key=value` label pair
77	(sorted by key) with `\n`:
78	
79	```
80	acme\nlatency_ms\nhost=a\nregion=eu
81	```
82	
83	`series_id = sha256(canonical_identity).hexdigest()`, so the same logical series
84	always maps to the same 64-character id, independent of label insertion order.
85	
86	Storage layout (all writes atomic via temp file + `os.replace`):
87	
88	```
89	<data-dir>/series.json              registry: series_id -> tenant/metric/labels
90	<data-dir>/points/<series_id>.jsonl one {"t":ts,"v":value} object per line
91	<data-dir>/quotas.json              tenant -> {"max_series","max_points"} limits
92	<data-dir>/rules.json               <data-dir>/alerts.json
93	<data-dir>/slos.json                <data-dir>/silences.json
94	<data-dir>/inhibitions.json         <data-dir>/counters.json
95	```
96	
97	A directory written before quotas existed simply has no `quotas.json`, which
98	means every tenant is unlimited; limits and usage are reloaded together on
99	construction so a reopen always reports a consistent snapshot.
100	
101	`SeriesStore` and `AlertEngine` each guard their state with a
102	`threading.RLock`, so the threaded HTTP server can serve concurrent requests; all
103	state is reloaded from disk on construction, so a restart preserves series,
104	points, rules, alerts, silences, inhibitions and SLOs.
105	
106	## Semantics and formulas
107	
108	**Idempotent write.** `write(tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None,
109	overwrite=False)` stores `(timestamp_ms, value)` pairs. Writing an existing
110	`(series, timestamp)` with the *same* value is a duplicate: it changes nothing
111	and is counted in `duplicates`. A *different* value for a stored timestamp is a
112	conflict: it raises `ObsError` (`409` over HTTP) unless `overwrite=True`, in
113	which case the stored value is replaced and counted in `written`. A timestamp
114	greater than the injected `now` (when `now` is given) is rejected.
115	
116	**Bucketing.** `query(..., step_ms=step, agg=agg)` assigns a sample with
117	timestamp `t` to bucket `b = t - (t % step)`, i.e. buckets are
118	left-closed/right-open (`[b, b+step)`) on epoch multiples. Every bucket from the
119	first non-empty bucket to the last non-empty bucket that also lies inside
120	`[start_ms, end_ms]` is emitted, and buckets with no sample are emitted as
121	`[b, null]`. Bucket value = `agg` over the samples in the bucket, where `agg` is
122	one of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`. A series whose range contains no
123	sample is still listed with an empty `points` list. With `agg` and *no*
124	`step_ms` the whole `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is a single bucket. With neither,
125	raw samples are returned in `[timestamp, value]` order. `rollup(tenant, metric,
126	labels, window_ms, agg)` is `query` with `step_ms = window_ms` over the whole
127	stored range, with empty buckets dropped; output is ordered by `series_id`, so
128	it is deterministic.
129	
130	**Label matchers.** In addition to exact `labels` / `label.k=v` filtering,
131	`query` accepts `matchers` (`matchers` on `GET /v1/query`, `--matchers` on the
132	CLI): a JSON array of objects containing exactly `key` (non-empty string),
133	`op` and `value` (string, may be empty). Ops are `=` / `!=` (exact whole-string
134	equality and negation) and `=~` / `!~` (Python `re` syntax matched against the
135	*whole* label value via full match, case-sensitive and Unicode-aware, and its
136	negation). Omitting the parameter, passing Python `None`, or sending `[]` adds
137	no condition; an explicit JSON `null` or empty text is rejected (HTTP/CLI).
138	Matchers combine with each other and with the exact label filters by logical
139	AND — including several matchers on the same key — apply to raw series labels
140	before bucketing or grouping (labels absent from `group_by` count too), and are
141	restricted to the requested `tenant` and `metric`; `tenant`, `metric` and
142	`series_id` are not implicit labels. A missing key never satisfies `=`/`=~` but
143	always satisfies `!=`/`!~`, so `=~ ""` selects only series where the key exists
144	with an empty value (grouping still separates a missing key from an empty
145	value). `api-.*` matches `api-a` but not `xapi-a`. Duplicate matchers never
146	duplicate series, matcher order is irrelevant, and contradictory matchers
147	yield an empty result. Invalid JSON, a non-array, non-object elements, missing
148	or extra fields, wrong types, an empty `key`, an unsupported `op` or an invalid
149	regex raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON error line on stderr for the
150	CLI); every matcher is validated even when no candidate series exists.
151	
152	**Grouped query.** `query(..., agg=agg, group_by=[keys...])` aggregates *across*
153	series: matching series (same tenant/metric/label filters and `[start_ms,
154	end_ms]` range as above) are bucketed into groups by the values of the given
155	label keys, and the raw in-range samples of all series in a group are pooled
156	before `agg` is applied — samples from different series at the same timestamp
157	count individually. `group_by=[]` merges every matching series into one group.
158	Each result row carries only `labels` (the group keys actually present on the
159	group's series — a missing key and an empty-string value form different
160	groups) and `points`; rows are ordered lexicographically by their sorted label
161	pairs. Bucketing follows the same rules as the per-series query (epoch-aligned
162	left-closed buckets with `null` gaps, or a single point at the group's
163	earliest sample without `step_ms`). A group whose series have no sample in
164	range is still listed with empty `points`; no matching series at all yields an
165	empty `series` array. `group_by` must be a list of distinct non-empty strings
166	and requires `agg`; violations raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON
167	error line on stderr for the CLI).
168	
169	**Sliding-window query.** `query(..., start_ms=start, end_ms=end, step_ms=step,
170	agg=agg, window_ms=window)` switches to a separate mode the moment `window_ms`
171	is supplied (it is optional in every binding: `window` on `GET /v1/query`,
172	`--window-ms` on the CLI). In this mode `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `step_ms` and
173	`agg` are all required; `start_ms` and `end_ms` must be integer milliseconds,
174	`step_ms` and `window_ms` positive integer milliseconds, and `end_ms >=
175	start_ms` (bools, fractions and missing/unknown values are rejected). Evaluation
176	times are `t = start + k*step` for `k = 0, 1, ...`, keeping only times
177	`t <= end`; the output point timestamp is the evaluation time itself. The step
178	need not divide the window and windows are never aligned to fixed buckets.
179	
180	Each evaluation aggregates the raw samples in the half-open interval
181	`(t - window_ms, t]`: the left edge is excluded (a sample exactly one window
182	length earlier does not count), the right edge included (a sample at `t`
183	does). `start_ms` only constrains the output grid — the first window at
184	`start` also reads history older than `start`; no window ever reads a sample
185	newer than its own evaluation time. The aggregation uses the same meanings as
186	bucketing (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`), and a window containing no
187	sample emits `[t, null]` for *every* aggregation, including `count`.
188	
189	Every matching registered series is returned on the full time grid even when
190	all of its windows are empty; no matching series yields an empty `series`
191	array. The Python per-series rows keep `series_id`; HTTP and CLI keep the
192	existing result shape. With `group_by`, all raw samples of the group's series
193	that fall in each window are pooled before aggregating (samples sharing a
194	timestamp across series count individually, `avg` divides by the total sample
195	count), a missing group key and an empty-string value stay distinct groups,
196	and each group keeps the full grid, fully null when no sample ever falls in a
197	window. Group filtering, ordering and validation follow the ordinary grouped
198	rules. The whole query reads one coherent snapshot, so concurrent writes or
199	retention sweeps can never mix old and new data; queries never alter samples,
200	counters or configuration, and the same history gives identical results after
201	reopening the store. Omitting `window_ms` preserves the previous query
202	behaviour exactly — `rollup`, write idempotency/overwrite, quotas, alerts and
203	SLOs are unaffected.
204	
205	**Retention.** `enforce_retention(tenant, cutoff_ms)` removes every sample of
206	that tenant with `timestamp_millis < cutoff_ms` and rewrites the affected point
207	files. `stats()` returns `{"series","points","writes","tenants"}`.
208	
209	**Per-tenant quotas.** `set_quota(tenant, max_series, max_points)` sets the
210	tenant-wide limits; each limit is a non-negative integer or `null` (omitted
211	fields over HTTP also mean `null`, i.e. unlimited), and `0` forbids adding any.
212	`get_quota(tenant)` returns
213	`{"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` — the configured
214	limits and the current usage in one snapshot. Configuring a quota never creates
215	a series, and an unconfigured tenant is unlimited. Limits apply to all of a
216	tenant's metrics together: `series` is the number of registered series and
217	`points` the total number of *distinct timestamps* across those series, not
218	physical point-file lines. Label order, same-value replays, overwritten points
219	and a timestamp repeated inside one batch add no occupancy.
220	
221	Every write path (`SeriesStore.write`, `POST /v1/series`, the CLI `write`) is
222	checked after the existing input validation and conflict rules, using the
223	batch's net increase: a batch is rejected (ObsError / HTTP `409` / CLI JSON
224	error with non-zero exit) when *either* dimension it increases would exceed its
225	limit, and the rejection leaves no new series, samples or write-count change.
226	Limits may be lowered below current usage; afterwards only the dimensions a
227	write actually increases are checked — an already-over-limit dimension blocks
228	nothing by itself, so pure duplicates and overwrites keep succeeding. Retention
229	frees the occupancy of deleted points, while empty series stay registered.
230	Overwrites rewrite the point file so one timestamp never occupies two lines; on
231	reopen, any duplicate timestamp lines (including those left by older builds)
232	collapse to the last value, so historical re-overwrites never double-count.
233	
234	**Rule shape.** `{"id","tenant","metric","labels","comparator" ∈ {">",">=","<",
235	"<=","==","!="},"threshold","for_ms","window_ms","agg","severity" ∈ {"info",
236	"warning","critical"},"annotations"}`. `add_rule` validates every field and
237	raises `ObsError` for anything malformed (`id` is generated when omitted).
238	
239	**Evaluation window.** Let `step = window_ms`, `t = now_ms` and
240	`bucket_start(t) = t - (t % step)`. The window is
241	`[bucket_start(t) - step, t]`, i.e. the current bucket plus the whole previous
242	bucket. The rule condition holds for a series when *every* non-empty bucket in
243	that window satisfies `comparator(value, threshold)` — one violating bucket
244	anywhere in the window stops the condition, and it keeps stopping it until that
245	bucket has left the window.
246	
247	**`for_ms`.** Let `run_start` be the timestamp of the first bucket of the
248	current unbroken run of satisfying buckets (a violating bucket resets the run).
249	The rule fires only when the condition holds *and*
250	`bucket_start(now_ms) - run_start >= for_ms`. With `for_ms = 0`, one satisfied
251	bucket is enough; with `for_ms = window_ms`, the current and the previous bucket
252	must both be satisfied. Before the hold time is reached the alert is recorded
253	with `firing = false` and appears in none of the four output lists.
254	
255	**Alert identity and dedup.** Alert identity is `(rule_id, series_id)`, distinct
256	from the alert id. The first time a condition holds an alert id
257	`alert-NNNNN` is minted for that identity and reused forever: re-evaluating an
258	unchanged condition returns the *same* `id` and increments `occurrences` (the
259	number of evaluations in which the condition held). `since_ms` is `run_start`,
260	not the evaluation time, so dedup does not depend on the wall clock.
261	
262	**Resolution.** When the condition stops holding, the alert's state becomes
263	`resolved`, `firing` becomes `false`, `resolved_ms` is set once, and the alert is
264	reported in the `resolved` list of that evaluation. If the same condition holds
265	again later, the *same alert id* is reused and `occurrences` keeps counting.
266	Because the condition covers the whole window, a series that produced one bad
267	bucket stays unresolved until that bucket has left the window.
268	
269	**Silence vs inhibition precedence.** A condition that holds and whose `for_ms`
270	is satisfied is first checked against active silences: a silence is active when
271	`starts_ms <= now_ms <= ends_ms`, the tenant matches and every silence label
272	matcher is present in the series labels. Inside an active silence the alert state
273	is `silenced` (it is *not* firing) and the silence id and reason are recorded.
274	Only if no silence matches is inhibition checked: an inhibition
275	`(source_severity, target_severity, same_labels)` marks a `target_severity` alert
276	as `inhibited` while an alert of at least `source_severity` is currently
277	`firing` in the same tenant with *exactly the same label set*. Silence therefore
278	wins over inhibition. A silenced or inhibited alert still counts its
279	`occurrences` and returns to `firing` as soon as the silence/inhibition no longer
280	applies. `list_alerts(state=None)` filters by `firing`, `silenced`, `inhibited`
281	or `resolved`.
282	
283	**SLO and error budget.** `set_slo(tenant, name, metric, labels,
284	good_comparator, threshold, target_ratio, window_ms)` defines a good-events
285	ratio SLO. `slo_status(name, now_ms, tenant=None)` counts every stored sample of
286	the matching series inside `[now_ms - window_ms, now_ms]`:
287	
288	```
289	total          = number of samples in the window (nulls excluded)
290	good           = samples where compare(value, good_comparator, threshold)
291	bad            = total - good
292	ratio          = good / total                             (0.0 when total == 0)
293	error_budget   = max(0.0, 1 - (1 - ratio) / (1 - target_ratio))   (target_ratio < 1)
294	               = 1.0 if ratio >= 1.0 else 0.0              (target_ratio == 1)
295	burn_rate      = (bad / total) / (1 - target_ratio)        (0.0 when target_ratio >= 1 or total == 0)
296	met            = ratio >= target_ratio
297	```
298	
299	`ratio` is the observed good ratio, `target_ratio ∈ (0,1]` the objective,
300	`burn_rate` how fast the budget is being spent relative to the allowed bad rate
301	(`1.0` means exactly on budget, `> 1.0` means burning too fast) and
302	`error_budget` the *fraction of the allowed error budget still unspent*:
303	`1.0` means untouched, `0.0` means exhausted or exceeded. For any `ratio` that
304	meets the target the two written forms of `error_budget` are identical, since
305	`1 - (1-ratio)/(1-target) = (ratio - target)/(1 - target)` and
306	`1 - ratio/target = (target - ratio)/target` are both non-negative only inside
307	their own regime; the first form is the one used, because it degrades sensibly
308	when the ratio beats the target (more budget left) instead of pinning to `0`.
309	With `total == 0` the ratio is `0.0`, so the budget counts as exhausted.
310	
311	Examples: 9 good + 1 bad with `target_ratio = 0.9` gives `ratio = 0.9`,
312	`error_budget = 0.0`, `burn_rate = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0`, `met = true` (exactly on
313	budget). 98 good + 2 bad with `target_ratio = 0.95` gives `ratio = 0.98`,
314	`burn_rate = 0.02/0.05 = 0.4` and `error_budget = 1 - 0.02/0.05 = 0.6` (60% of
315	the budget still unspent). 90 good + 10 bad with `target_ratio = 0.99` gives
316	`ratio = 0.9`, `burn_rate = 10.0`, `error_budget = 0.0`, `met = false`.
317	
318	**Determinism.** No module calls `time.time()` inside decision logic: `now_ms` is
319	passed into `evaluate`, `slo_status` and `write` (the HTTP layer uses the wall
320	clock only when a caller omits `now_ms` on `GET /v1/slos/status`, and

322	
323	## Layout
324	
325	```
326	obsd/__init__.py    public exports
327	obsd/tsdb.py        SeriesStore
328	obsd/alerts.py      AlertEngine
329	obsd/http_app.py    ThreadingHTTPServer + create_server
330	obsd/cli.py         command line interface
331	obsd/__main__.py    python3 -m obsd entry point
332	tests/              unittest suite (tsdb, alerts, http)
333	```
334	
335	## Tests

339	```

342	conflicting-timestamp rejection and `overwrite`, range filtering, epoch-aligned

# obsd

Minimal, dependency-free backend skeleton for **metrics ingestion, alerting and
SLO tracking**. Python 3.10+, standard library only, offline, deterministic
(every time-dependent entry point takes an injected `now_ms`).

The lane goal is a metrics collection, alerting and SLO backend that grows
towards time-series writes and downsampling, label indexing and a query subset,
aggregation and sliding windows, alert rules with silencing and inhibition,
notification routing and dedup, SLO and error-budget math, retention and
compaction, multi-tenant quota, access control and audit, and consistent reads
under high availability. This seed implements the first, smallest *real* slice of
each of those areas.

## Run

```bash
# HTTP API (data dir flag is global and comes BEFORE the subcommand)
python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

# test suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both commands are run offline with the system interpreter; no third-party
package is imported anywhere.

## CLI

`python3 -m obsd [--data-dir ./obsd_data] <command> ...` prints exactly one line
of JSON on stdout. On error it prints one line of JSON (`{"error":"..."}`) on
stderr and exits non-zero.

| Command | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `serve` | `python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` |
| `quota-set` | `python3 -m obsd quota-set --tenant acme --max-series 1000 --max-points 1000000` |
| `quota-get` | `python3 -m obsd quota-get --tenant acme` |
| `write` | `python3 -m obsd write --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --label host=a --sample 1000:12.5 --now-ms 2000` |
| `query` | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --agg avg` |
| `query` (grouped) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --agg avg --group-by '["host"]'` |
| `query` (matchers) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --matchers '[{"key":"host","op":"=~","value":"api-.*"}]'` |
| `query` (sliding window) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --window-ms 5000 --agg avg` |
| `rule-add` | `python3 -m obsd rule-add --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --comparator "<" --threshold 10 --window-ms 60000 --for-ms 30000 --agg avg --severity warning` |
| `eval` | `python3 -m obsd eval --now-ms 68000` |
| `alerts` | `python3 -m obsd alerts --tenant acme --state firing` |
| `silence-add` | `python3 -m obsd silence-add --tenant acme --starts-ms 0 --ends-ms 90000 --reason maintenance` |
| `slo set` | `python3 -m obsd slo set --tenant acme --name availability --metric latency_ms --good-comparator ">=" --threshold 1 --target-ratio 0.9 --window-ms 60000` |
| `slo status` | `python3 -m obsd slo status --name availability --now-ms 60000` |

## HTTP API

Errors are always JSON: `{"error":"..."}` with status 400 (bad request),
404 (unknown resource) or 409 (write conflict or quota exceeded).

| Method | Path | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/healthz` | – | `200 {"ok":true}` |
| POST | `/v1/series` | `{"tenant","metric","labels","samples":[[ts,value],...]}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"series_id":"..."}`, `409` on conflicting timestamp or quota exceeded |
| GET | `/v1/query` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&step=&agg=&group_by=&window=&matchers=` (group_by and matchers are JSON arrays; matchers holds `{"key","op","value"}` objects) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}` |
| POST | `/v1/quotas` | `{"tenant","max_series":n\|null,"max_points":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/limits give `400` and leave config untouched |
| GET | `/v1/quotas` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports `null` limits and real usage) |
| POST | `/v1/rules` | rule object | `201` stored rule |
| GET | `/v1/rules` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"rules":[...]}` |
| POST | `/v1/evaluate` | `{"now_ms":n}` | `200 {"firing":[...],"silenced":[...],"inhibited":[...],"resolved":[...]}` |
| GET | `/v1/alerts` | `?tenant=&state=` | `200 {"alerts":[...]}` |
| POST | `/v1/silences` | `{"tenant","labels","starts_ms","ends_ms","reason"}` | `201` stored silence |
| POST | `/v1/inhibitions` | `{"source_severity","target_severity","same_labels"}` | `201` stored inhibition |
| POST | `/v1/slos` | `{"tenant","name","metric","labels","good_comparator","threshold","target_ratio","window_ms"}` | `201` stored SLO |
| GET | `/v1/slos/status` | `?tenant=&name=&now_ms=` | `200` SLO status object |
| GET | `/v1/stats` | – | `200 {"store":{...},"alerts":n}` |

## Data model

A series identity is `(tenant, metric, sorted(label pairs))`. The canonical
identity string joins the tenant, the metric and every `key=value` label pair
(sorted by key) with `\n`:

```
acme\nlatency_ms\nhost=a\nregion=eu
```

`series_id = sha256(canonical_identity).hexdigest()`, so the same logical series
always maps to the same 64-character id, independent of label insertion order.

Storage layout (all writes atomic via temp file + `os.replace`):

```
<data-dir>/series.json              registry: series_id -> tenant/metric/labels
<data-dir>/points/<series_id>.jsonl one {"t":ts,"v":value} object per line
<data-dir>/quotas.json              tenant -> {"max_series","max_points"} limits
<data-dir>/rules.json               <data-dir>/alerts.json
<data-dir>/slos.json                <data-dir>/silences.json
<data-dir>/inhibitions.json         <data-dir>/counters.json
```

A directory written before quotas existed simply has no `quotas.json`, which
means every tenant is unlimited; limits and usage are reloaded together on
construction so a reopen always reports a consistent snapshot.

`SeriesStore` and `AlertEngine` each guard their state with a
`threading.RLock`, so the threaded HTTP server can serve concurrent requests; all
state is reloaded from disk on construction, so a restart preserves series,
points, rules, alerts, silences, inhibitions and SLOs.

## Semantics and formulas

**Idempotent write.** `write(tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None,
overwrite=False)` stores `(timestamp_ms, value)` pairs. Writing an existing
`(series, timestamp)` with the *same* value is a duplicate: it changes nothing
and is counted in `duplicates`. A *different* value for a stored timestamp is a
conflict: it raises `ObsError` (`409` over HTTP) unless `overwrite=True`, in
which case the stored value is replaced and counted in `written`. A timestamp
greater than the injected `now` (when `now` is given) is rejected.

**Bucketing.** `query(..., step_ms=step, agg=agg)` assigns a sample with
timestamp `t` to bucket `b = t - (t % step)`, i.e. buckets are
left-closed/right-open (`[b, b+step)`) on epoch multiples. Every bucket from the
first non-empty bucket to the last non-empty bucket that also lies inside
`[start_ms, end_ms]` is emitted, and buckets with no sample are emitted as
`[b, null]`. Bucket value = `agg` over the samples in the bucket, where `agg` is
one of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`. A series whose range contains no
sample is still listed with an empty `points` list. With `agg` and *no*
`step_ms` the whole `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is a single bucket. With neither,
raw samples are returned in `[timestamp, value]` order. `rollup(tenant, metric,
labels, window_ms, agg)` is `query` with `step_ms = window_ms` over the whole
stored range, with empty buckets dropped; output is ordered by `series_id`, so
it is deterministic.

**Label matchers.** In addition to exact `labels` / `label.k=v` filtering,
`query` accepts `matchers` (`matchers` on `GET /v1/query`, `--matchers` on the
CLI): a JSON array of objects containing exactly `key` (non-empty string),
`op` and `value` (string, may be empty). Ops are `=` / `!=` (exact whole-string
equality and negation) and `=~` / `!~` (Python `re` syntax matched against the
*whole* label value via full match, case-sensitive and Unicode-aware, and its
negation). Omitting the parameter, passing Python `None`, or sending `[]` adds
no condition; an explicit JSON `null` or empty text is rejected (HTTP/CLI).
Matchers combine with each other and with the exact label filters by logical
AND — including several matchers on the same key — apply to raw series labels
before bucketing or grouping (labels absent from `group_by` count too), and are
restricted to the requested `tenant` and `metric`; `tenant`, `metric` and
`series_id` are not implicit labels. A missing key never satisfies `=`/`=~` but
always satisfies `!=`/`!~`, so `=~ ""` selects only series where the key exists
with an empty value (grouping still separates a missing key from an empty
value). `api-.*` matches `api-a` but not `xapi-a`. Duplicate matchers never
duplicate series, matcher order is irrelevant, and contradictory matchers
yield an empty result. Invalid JSON, a non-array, non-object elements, missing
or extra fields, wrong types, an empty `key`, an unsupported `op` or an invalid
regex raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON error line on stderr for the
CLI); every matcher is validated even when no candidate series exists.

**Grouped query.** `query(..., agg=agg, group_by=[keys...])` aggregates *across*
series: matching series (same tenant/metric/label filters and `[start_ms,
end_ms]` range as above) are bucketed into groups by the values of the given
label keys, and the raw in-range samples of all series in a group are pooled
before `agg` is applied — samples from different series at the same timestamp
count individually. `group_by=[]` merges every matching series into one group.
Each result row carries only `labels` (the group keys actually present on the
group's series — a missing key and an empty-string value form different
groups) and `points`; rows are ordered lexicographically by their sorted label
pairs. Bucketing follows the same rules as the per-series query (epoch-aligned
left-closed buckets with `null` gaps, or a single point at the group's
earliest sample without `step_ms`). A group whose series have no sample in
range is still listed with empty `points`; no matching series at all yields an
empty `series` array. `group_by` must be a list of distinct non-empty strings
and requires `agg`; violations raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON
error line on stderr for the CLI).

**Sliding-window query.** `query(..., start_ms=start, end_ms=end, step_ms=step,
agg=agg, window_ms=window)` switches to a separate mode the moment `window_ms`
is supplied (it is optional in every binding: `window` on `GET /v1/query`,
`--window-ms` on the CLI). In this mode `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `step_ms` and
`agg` are all required; `start_ms` and `end_ms` must be integer milliseconds,
`step_ms` and `window_ms` positive integer milliseconds, and `end_ms >=
start_ms` (bools, fractions and missing/unknown values are rejected). Evaluation
times are `t = start + k*step` for `k = 0, 1, ...`, keeping only times
`t <= end`; the output point timestamp is the evaluation time itself. The step
need not divide the window and windows are never aligned to fixed buckets.

Each evaluation aggregates the raw samples in the half-open interval
`(t - window_ms, t]`: the left edge is excluded (a sample exactly one window
length earlier does not count), the right edge included (a sample at `t`
does). `start_ms` only constrains the output grid — the first window at
`start` also reads history older than `start`; no window ever reads a sample
newer than its own evaluation time. The aggregation uses the same meanings as
bucketing (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`), and a window containing no
sample emits `[t, null]` for *every* aggregation, including `count`.

Every matching registered series is returned on the full time grid even when
all of its windows are empty; no matching series yields an empty `series`
array. The Python per-series rows keep `series_id`; HTTP and CLI keep the
existing result shape. With `group_by`, all raw samples of the group's series
that fall in each window are pooled before aggregating (samples sharing a
timestamp across series count individually, `avg` divides by the total sample
count), a missing group key and an empty-string value stay distinct groups,
and each group keeps the full grid, fully null when no sample ever falls in a
window. Group filtering, ordering and validation follow the ordinary grouped
rules. The whole query reads one coherent snapshot, so concurrent writes or
retention sweeps can never mix old and new data; queries never alter samples,
counters or configuration, and the same history gives identical results after
reopening the store. Omitting `window_ms` preserves the previous query
behaviour exactly — `rollup`, write idempotency/overwrite, quotas, alerts and
SLOs are unaffected.

**Retention.** `enforce_retention(tenant, cutoff_ms)` removes every sample of
that tenant with `timestamp_millis < cutoff_ms` and rewrites the affected point
files. `stats()` returns `{"series","points","writes","tenants"}`.

**Per-tenant quotas.** `set_quota(tenant, max_series, max_points)` sets the
tenant-wide limits; each limit is a non-negative integer or `null` (omitted
fields over HTTP also mean `null`, i.e. unlimited), and `0` forbids adding any.
`get_quota(tenant)` returns
`{"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` — the configured
limits and the current usage in one snapshot. Configuring a quota never creates
a series, and an unconfigured tenant is unlimited. Limits apply to all of a
tenant's metrics together: `series` is the number of registered series and
`points` the total number of *distinct timestamps* across those series, not
physical point-file lines. Label order, same-value replays, overwritten points
and a timestamp repeated inside one batch add no occupancy.

Every write path (`SeriesStore.write`, `POST /v1/series`, the CLI `write`) is
checked after the existing input validation and conflict rules, using the
batch's net increase: a batch is rejected (ObsError / HTTP `409` / CLI JSON
error with non-zero exit) when *either* dimension it increases would exceed its
limit, and the rejection leaves no new series, samples or write-count change.
Limits may be lowered below current usage; afterwards only the dimensions a
write actually increases are checked — an already-over-limit dimension blocks
nothing by itself, so pure duplicates and overwrites keep succeeding. Retention
frees the occupancy of deleted points, while empty series stay registered.
Overwrites rewrite the point file so one timestamp never occupies two lines; on
reopen, any duplicate timestamp lines (including those left by older builds)
collapse to the last value, so historical re-overwrites never double-count.

**Rule shape.** `{"id","tenant","metric","labels","comparator" ∈ {">",">=","<",
"<=","==","!="},"threshold","for_ms","window_ms","agg","severity" ∈ {"info",
"warning","critical"},"annotations"}`. `add_rule` validates every field and
raises `ObsError` for anything malformed (`id` is generated when omitted).

**Evaluation window.** Let `step = window_ms`, `t = now_ms` and
`bucket_start(t) = t - (t % step)`. The window is
`[bucket_start(t) - step, t]`, i.e. the current bucket plus the whole previous
bucket. The rule condition holds for a series when *every* non-empty bucket in
that window satisfies `comparator(value, threshold)` — one violating bucket
anywhere in the window stops the condition, and it keeps stopping it until that
bucket has left the window.

**`for_ms`.** Let `run_start` be the timestamp of the first bucket of the
current unbroken run of satisfying buckets (a violating bucket resets the run).
The rule fires only when the condition holds *and*
`bucket_start(now_ms) - run_start >= for_ms`. With `for_ms = 0`, one satisfied
bucket is enough; with `for_ms = window_ms`, the current and the previous bucket
must both be satisfied. Before the hold time is reached the alert is recorded
with `firing = false` and appears in none of the four output lists.

**Alert identity and dedup.** Alert identity is `(rule_id, series_id)`, distinct
from the alert id. The first time a condition holds an alert id
`alert-NNNNN` is minted for that identity and reused forever: re-evaluating an
unchanged condition returns the *same* `id` and increments `occurrences` (the
number of evaluations in which the condition held). `since_ms` is `run_start`,
not the evaluation time, so dedup does not depend on the wall clock.

**Resolution.** When the condition stops holding, the alert's state becomes
`resolved`, `firing` becomes `false`, `resolved_ms` is set once, and the alert is
reported in the `resolved` list of that evaluation. If the same condition holds
again later, the *same alert id* is reused and `occurrences` keeps counting.
Because the condition covers the whole window, a series that produced one bad
bucket stays unresolved until that bucket has left the window.

**Silence vs inhibition precedence.** A condition that holds and whose `for_ms`
is satisfied is first checked against active silences: a silence is active when
`starts_ms <= now_ms <= ends_ms`, the tenant matches and every silence label
matcher is present in the series labels. Inside an active silence the alert state
is `silenced` (it is *not* firing) and the silence id and reason are recorded.
Only if no silence matches is inhibition checked: an inhibition
`(source_severity, target_severity, same_labels)` marks a `target_severity` alert
as `inhibited` while an alert of at least `source_severity` is currently
`firing` in the same tenant with *exactly the same label set*. Silence therefore
wins over inhibition. A silenced or inhibited alert still counts its
`occurrences` and returns to `firing` as soon as the silence/inhibition no longer
applies. `list_alerts(state=None)` filters by `firing`, `silenced`, `inhibited`
or `resolved`.

**SLO and error budget.** `set_slo(tenant, name, metric, labels,
good_comparator, threshold, target_ratio, window_ms)` defines a good-events
ratio SLO. `slo_status(name, now_ms, tenant=None)` counts every stored sample of
the matching series inside `[now_ms - window_ms, now_ms]`:

```
total          = number of samples in the window (nulls excluded)
good           = samples where compare(value, good_comparator, threshold)
bad            = total - good
ratio          = good / total                             (0.0 when total == 0)
error_budget   = max(0.0, 1 - (1 - ratio) / (1 - target_ratio))   (target_ratio < 1)
               = 1.0 if ratio >= 1.0 else 0.0              (target_ratio == 1)
burn_rate      = (bad / total) / (1 - target_ratio)        (0.0 when target_ratio >= 1 or total == 0)
met            = ratio >= target_ratio
```

`ratio` is the observed good ratio, `target_ratio ∈ (0,1]` the objective,
`burn_rate` how fast the budget is being spent relative to the allowed bad rate
(`1.0` means exactly on budget, `> 1.0` means burning too fast) and
`error_budget` the *fraction of the allowed error budget still unspent*:
`1.0` means untouched, `0.0` means exhausted or exceeded. For any `ratio` that
meets the target the two written forms of `error_budget` are identical, since
`1 - (1-ratio)/(1-target) = (ratio - target)/(1 - target)` and
`1 - ratio/target = (target - ratio)/target` are both non-negative only inside
their own regime; the first form is the one used, because it degrades sensibly
when the ratio beats the target (more budget left) instead of pinning to `0`.
With `total == 0` the ratio is `0.0`, so the budget counts as exhausted.

Examples: 9 good + 1 bad with `target_ratio = 0.9` gives `ratio = 0.9`,
`error_budget = 0.0`, `burn_rate = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0`, `met = true` (exactly on
budget). 98 good + 2 bad with `target_ratio = 0.95` gives `ratio = 0.98`,
`burn_rate = 0.02/0.05 = 0.4` and `error_budget = 1 - 0.02/0.05 = 0.6` (60% of
the budget still unspent). 90 good + 10 bad with `target_ratio = 0.99` gives
`ratio = 0.9`, `burn_rate = 10.0`, `error_budget = 0.0`, `met = false`.

**Determinism.** No module calls `time.time()` inside decision logic: `now_ms` is
passed into `evaluate`, `slo_status` and `write` (the HTTP layer uses the wall
clock only when a caller omits `now_ms` on `GET /v1/slos/status`, and
`/v1/slos/status` requires it in the CLI).

## Layout

```

obsd/tsdb.py        SeriesStore

obsd/http_app.py    ThreadingHTTPServer + create_server
obsd/cli.py         command line interface
obsd/__main__.py    python3 -m obsd entry point
tests/              unittest suite (tsdb, alerts, http)
```

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Covered: series identity and label-order independence, idempotent re-write,
conflicting-timestamp rejection and `overwrite`, range filtering, epoch-aligned

sliding-window grids with left-open/right-closed windows, null empty windows

30	    """Normalise labels to a list of ``[key, value]`` pairs sorted by key."""
31	    if labels is None:
32	        return []
33	    if isinstance(labels, dict):
34	        items = list(labels.items())
35	    elif isinstance(labels, (list, tuple)):
36	        items = []
37	        for entry in labels:
38	            if not isinstance(entry, (list, tuple)) or len(entry) != 2:
39	                raise ObsError("labels entries must be [key, value] pairs")
40	            items.append((entry[0], entry[1]))
41	    else:
42	        raise ObsError("labels must be an object or a list of pairs")
43	    pairs = []
44	    for key, value in items:
45	        if not isinstance(key, str) or value is None:
46	            raise ObsError("label keys must be strings and values must not be null")
47	        pairs.append([key, str(value)])
48	    pairs.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])
49	    if len({key for key, _ in pairs}) != len(pairs):
50	        raise ObsError("duplicate label key")
51	    return pairs

74	def matches_labels(series_labels, matcher):
75	    """True when every matcher pair is present in ``series_labels``."""
76	    if not matcher:
77	        return True
78	    if isinstance(matcher, (list, tuple)):
79	        matcher = as_labels(matcher)

83	def compile_matchers(matchers):
84	    """Validate ``matchers`` and return ``(key, op, value, pattern)`` tuples.
85	
86	    Each element is an object with exactly ``key`` (non-empty string), ``op``
87	    (one of ``=``, ``!=``, ``=~``, ``!~``) and ``value`` (string, possibly
88	    empty). ``None`` and an empty list add no condition; regex patterns are
89	    compiled here, so an invalid pattern is rejected before any series is read.
90	    """
91	    if matchers is None:
92	        return ()
93	    if not isinstance(matchers, (list, tuple)):
94	        raise ObsError("matchers must be a list of matcher objects")
95	    compiled = []
96	    for element in matchers:
97	        if not isinstance(element, dict):
98	            raise ObsError("each matcher must be an object with key, op and value")
99	        if set(element) != {"key", "op", "value"}:
100	            raise ObsError("each matcher must contain exactly key, op and value")
101	        key, op, value = element["key"], element["op"], element["value"]
102	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
103	            raise ObsError("matcher key must be a non-empty string")
104	        if op not in MATCHER_OPS:
105	            raise ObsError("matcher op must be one of %s" % (MATCHER_OPS,))
106	        if not isinstance(value, str):
107	            raise ObsError("matcher value must be a string")
108	        pattern = None
109	        if op in ("=~", "!~"):
110	            try:
111	                pattern = re.compile(value)
112	            except re.error as exc:
113	                raise ObsError("invalid matcher regex %r: %s" % (value, exc))
114	        compiled.append((key, op, value, pattern))
115	    return tuple(compiled)
116

118	def matchers_hold(series_labels, compiled):
119	    """True when every compiled matcher holds for ``series_labels``.
120	
121	    A missing key never satisfies ``=``/``=~`` but always satisfies ``!=``/
122	    ``!~``; regex matchers anchor with ``fullmatch`` so the pattern covers the
123	    whole value. Only real labels are considered.
124	    """
125	    for key, op, value, pattern in compiled:
126	        present = key in series_labels
127	        if op == "=":
128	            if not present or series_labels[key] != value:
129	                return False
130	        elif op == "!=":
131	            if present and series_labels[key] == value:
132	                return False
133	        elif op == "=~":
134	            if not present or pattern.fullmatch(series_labels[key]) is None:
135	                return False
136	        else:  # "!~"
137	            if present and pattern.fullmatch(series_labels[key]) is not None:
138	                return False
139	    return True

142	def parse_matchers_text(text, field="matchers"):
143	    """Decode a JSON array text of matcher objects; ``None``/absent adds none.
144	
145	    Used by the HTTP and CLI entry points, where the parameter arrives as a
146	    string. Returns the raw decoded list (validated later by
147	    :func:`compile_matchers`, which runs even with no candidate series). Empty
148	    text and an explicit JSON ``null`` are illegal here (unlike omitting the
149	    parameter or passing Python ``None`` to ``query``).
150	    """
151	    if text is None:
152	        return None
153	    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text:
154	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
155	    try:
156	        data = json.loads(text)
157	    except ValueError:
158	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
159	    if data is None:
160	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
161	    if not isinstance(data, list):
162	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
163	    return data

166	def _aggregate(values, agg):
167	    if agg == "sum":
168	        return float(sum(values))
169	    if agg == "avg":
170	        return sum(values) / float(len(values))
171	    if agg == "min":
172	        return float(min(values))
173	    if agg == "max":
174	        return float(max(values))
175	    if agg == "count":
176	        return len(values)
177	    raise ObsError("unknown aggregation: %r" % (agg,))

180	def _atomic_write(path, text):
181	    """Write ``text`` to ``path`` through a temp file plus os.replace."""
182	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
183	    if directory:
184	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
185	    with open(path + ".tmp", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
186	        handle.write(text)
187	        handle.flush()
188	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
189	    os.replace(path + ".tmp", path)

196	class SeriesStore:
197	    """Append-mostly time series store persisted under ``root``.
198	
199	    Layout::
200	
201	        <root>/series.json                 registry: series_id -> series row
202	        <root>/points/<series_id>.jsonl    one ``{"t":ts,"v":value}`` per line
203	        <root>/quotas.json                 tenant -> {"max_series", "max_points"}
204	    """
205	
206	    def __init__(self, root):
207	        if not isinstance(root, (str, os.PathLike)) or not str(root):
208	            raise ObsError("root must be a non-empty path")
209	        self.root = os.path.abspath(str(root))
210	        self.points_dir = os.path.join(self.root, "points")
211	        self.series_path = os.path.join(self.root, "series.json")
212	        self.quota_path = os.path.join(self.root, "quotas.json")
213	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
214	        self._series, self._samples, self._writes = {}, {}, 0
215	        self._quotas = {}
216	        os.makedirs(self.points_dir, exist_ok=True)
217	        self._load()
218	        self._load_quotas()
219	
220	    def _points_path(self, sid):
221	        return os.path.join(self.points_dir, sid + ".jsonl")
222	
223	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- persistence
224	    def _load(self):
225	        rows = []
226	        if os.path.exists(self.series_path):
227	            try:
228	                with open(self.series_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
229	                    rows = json.load(handle)
230	            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
231	                raise ObsError("cannot read series registry: %s" % exc)
232	        for row in rows:
233	            sid = row.get("series_id")
234	            if not sid:
235	                continue
236	            self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": row.get("tenant"),
237	                                 "metric": row.get("metric"),
238	                                 "labels": [[str(k), str(v)] for k, v in row.get("labels", [])],
239	                                 "identity": row.get("identity")}
240	            self._samples[sid] = self._read_points(sid)
241	
242	    def _read_points(self, sid):
243	        """Reload one point file, skipping unreadable lines.
244	
245	        Repeated lines for the same timestamp (left behind by historical
246	        overwrites) collapse to the last value stored, so occupancy counts each
247	        distinct timestamp once after a reopen.
248	        """
249	        rows = {}
250	        path = self._points_path(sid)
251	        if os.path.exists(path):
252	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
253	                for line in handle:
254	                    try:
255	                        row = json.loads(line)
256	                        rows[int(row["t"])] = float(row["v"])
257	                    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
258	                        continue
259	        return sorted(rows.items())
260	
261	    def _save_registry(self):
262	        _atomic_write(self.series_path, json.dumps(
263	            [self._series[sid] for sid in sorted(self._series)],
264	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
265	
266	    def _rewrite_points(self, sid):
267	        _atomic_write(self._points_path(sid),
268	                      "".join(_line(ts, value) for ts, value in self._samples[sid]))
269	
270	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ quotas
271	    def _load_quotas(self):
272	        """Reload ``quotas.json``; a missing file means every tenant is unlimited."""
273	        if not os.path.exists(self.quota_path):
274	            return
275	        try:
276	            with open(self.quota_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
277	                data = json.load(handle)
278	        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
279	            raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: %s" % exc)
280	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
281	            raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: root must be an object")
282	        for tenant, row in data.items():
283	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant or not isinstance(row, dict):
284	                raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: malformed entry")
285	            self._quotas[tenant] = {
286	                "max_series": self._clean_limit(row.get("max_series"), "max_series"),
287	                "max_points": self._clean_limit(row.get("max_points"), "max_points")}
288	
289	    @staticmethod
290	    def _clean_limit(value, field):
291	        """A limit is a non-negative integer or ``None`` (unlimited)."""
292	        if value is None:
293	            return None
294	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
295	            raise ObsError("%s must be a non-negative integer or null" % field)
296	        if value < 0:
297	            raise ObsError("%s must be a non-negative integer or null" % field)
298	        return value
299	
300	    @staticmethod
301	    def _clean_tenant(tenant):
302	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant:
303	            raise ObsError("tenant must be a non-empty string")
304	        return tenant
305	
306	    def _save_quotas(self):
307	        _atomic_write(self.quota_path, json.dumps(
308	            {tenant: self._quotas[tenant] for tenant in sorted(self._quotas)},
309	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
310	
311	    def set_quota(self, tenant, max_series, max_points):
312	        """Configure the per-tenant limits; ``None`` means unlimited.
313	
314	        Limits may be lowered below current usage; pure duplicate/overwrite
315	        writes stay allowed afterwards. Configuring a quota never creates a
316	        series.
317	        """
318	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
319	        max_series = self._clean_limit(max_series, "max_series")
320	        max_points = self._clean_limit(max_points, "max_points")
321	        with self._lock:
322	            self._quotas[tenant] = {"max_series": max_series, "max_points": max_points}
323	            self._save_quotas()
324	            return self.get_quota(tenant)
325	
326	    def get_quota(self, tenant):
327	        """Return limits and current usage for ``tenant`` in one snapshot."""
328	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
329	        with self._lock:
330	            limits = self._quotas.get(tenant, {"max_series": None, "max_points": None})
331	            series = points = 0
332	            for sid, row in self._series.items():
333	                if row["tenant"] == tenant:
334	                    series += 1
335	                    points += len(self._samples[sid])
336	            return {"tenant": tenant, "max_series": limits["max_series"],
337	                    "max_points": limits["max_points"], "series": series, "points": points}
338	
339	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- write
340	    def write(self, tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None, overwrite=False):
341	        """Store ``samples`` = ``[(timestamp_ms, value), ...]``.
342	
343	        Idempotent: an identical ``(series, timestamp)`` value is a duplicate
344	        and changes nothing. A differing value for a stored timestamp raises
345	        ``ObsError`` unless ``overwrite=True``.
346	
347	        The whole batch is checked against the tenant's configured quotas
348	        *after* input validation and conflict rules, using the net new series
349	        and distinct new timestamps the batch would add (same-value replays,
350	        overwrites and timestamps repeated inside the batch add nothing). A
351	        batch that would exceed either limit is rejected wholesale with
352	        ``ObsError``: no series, points or write counter change is kept.
353	        """
354	        if not isinstance(samples, (list, tuple)):
355	            raise ObsError("samples must be a list of [timestamp_ms, value] pairs")
356	        clean = []
357	        for entry in samples:
358	            if not isinstance(entry, (list, tuple)) or len(entry) != 2:
359	                raise ObsError("each sample must be a [timestamp_ms, value] pair")
360	            stamp, value = entry
361	            if not _num(stamp) or not _num(value):
362	                raise ObsError("sample timestamp and value must be numbers")
363	            if now is not None and int(stamp) > int(now):
364	                raise ObsError("sample timestamp %d is in the future (now=%d)"
365	                               % (int(stamp), int(now)))
366	            clean.append((int(stamp), float(value)))
367	        if not clean:
368	            raise ObsError("samples must not be empty")
369	        # Labels/tenant are validated before the lock so conflicts and quota
370	        # breaches never surface as identity errors.
371	        pairs = _labels_list(labels)
372	        identity = canonical_identity(tenant, metric, pairs)
373	        sid = hashlib.sha256(identity.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
374	        with self._lock:
375	            existed = sid in self._series
376	            current = dict(self._samples.get(sid, ()))
377	            merged = dict(current)
378	            written = duplicates = 0
379	            new_stamps = set()
380	            overwritten = False
381	            for stamp, value in clean:
382	                if stamp in merged:
383	                    if merged[stamp] != value:
384	                        if not overwrite:
385	                            raise ObsError(
386	                                "conflict for %s at timestamp %d: stored=%r incoming=%r"
387	                                % (sid, stamp, merged[stamp], value))
388	                        if stamp in current:
389	                            overwritten = True
390	                    else:
391	                        duplicates += 1
392	                        continue
393	                else:
394	                    new_stamps.add(stamp)
395	                merged[stamp] = value
396	                written += 1
397	
398	            quota = self._quotas.get(tenant)
399	            if quota is not None:
400	                used_series = used_points = 0
401	                for sid_, row in self._series.items():
402	                    if row["tenant"] == tenant:
403	                        used_series += 1
404	                        used_points += len(self._samples[sid_])
405	                new_series = 0 if existed else 1
406	                new_points = len(new_stamps)
407	                limit_series = quota["max_series"]
408	                limit_points = quota["max_points"]
409	                if new_series and limit_series is not None \
410	                        and used_series + new_series > limit_series:
411	                    raise ObsError(
412	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: series %d+%d > max_series %s"
413	                        % (tenant, used_series, new_series, limit_series))
414	                if new_points and limit_points is not None \
415	                        and used_points + new_points > limit_points:
416	                    raise ObsError(
417	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: points %d+%d > max_points %s"
418	                        % (tenant, used_points, new_points, limit_points))
419	
420	            if not existed:
421	                self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": tenant, "metric": metric,
422	                                     "labels": pairs, "identity": identity}
423	                self._samples[sid] = []
424	            if written:
425	                self._samples[sid] = sorted(merged.items())
426	                if overwritten:
427	                    # An overwrite replaced a stored value: rewrite the file so a
428	                    # timestamp never occupies more than one physical line.
429	                    self._rewrite_points(sid)
430	                else:
431	                    fresh = sorted((stamp, merged[stamp]) for stamp in new_stamps)
432	                    with open(self._points_path(sid), "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
433	                        handle.write("".join(_line(ts, value) for ts, value in fresh))
434	                        handle.flush()
435	                        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
436	                self._writes += 1
437	                self._save_registry()
438	        return {"series_id": sid, "written": written, "duplicates": duplicates}
439	
440	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- query
441	    def _matching_series(self, tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers=()):
442	        """Snapshot of every matching series: sid, labels and raw samples.
443	
444	        Copied under one lock acquisition so a query can never mix samples from
445	        before and after a concurrent write or retention sweep. Exact ``labels``
446	        and the compiled ``matchers`` both filter the same raw series labels
447	        before any aggregation or grouping takes place.
448	        """
449	        with self._lock:
450	            ids = sorted(sid for sid, row in self._series.items()
451	                         if row["tenant"] == tenant and row["metric"] == metric
452	                         and matches_labels(dict(row["labels"]), labels)
453	                         and matchers_hold(dict(row["labels"]), compiled_matchers))
454	            return [(sid, dict(self._series[sid]["labels"]), list(self._samples[sid]))
455	                    for sid in ids]
456	
457	    def _samples_for(self, tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers=()):
458	        return [(sid, samples) for sid, _, samples in
459	                self._matching_series(tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers)]
460	
461	    def _scan(self, tenant, metric, labels, start_ms, end_ms):
462	        """Raw samples of matching series inside ``[start, end]`` (internal).
463	
464	        Used where exact event counts matter (SLO numerator/denominator) and by
465	        rule evaluation to find candidate series.
466	        """
467	        lo = None if start_ms is None else int(start_ms)
468	        hi = None if end_ms is None else int(end_ms)
469	        out = []
470	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels):
471	            rows = [item for item in samples
472	                    if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo) and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi)]
473	            if rows:
474	                out.append((sid, rows))
475	        return out
476	
477	    def query(self, tenant, metric, labels=None, start_ms=None, end_ms=None,
478	              step_ms=None, agg=None, group_by=None, window_ms=None, matchers=None):
479	        """Raw, bucketed or sliding-window points per matching series.
480	
481	        ``matchers`` is an optional list of ``{"key", "op", "value"}`` objects
482	        (``None`` or ``[]`` adds no condition). Supported ops: ``=``, ``!=``
483	        (exact whole-string equality/negation), ``=~``, ``!~`` (Python ``re``
484	        full-match/negation, case-sensitive, Unicode-aware). Matchers combine
485	        with each other and with ``labels`` by logical AND, apply to the raw
486	        series labels before bucketing/grouping (keys absent from
487	        ``group_by`` included), and are validated up front even when no series
488	        could match. A missing key fails ``=``/``=~`` and passes ``!=``/``!~``.
489	
490	        ``step_ms`` buckets are left-closed/right-open on epoch multiples and
491	        empty buckets are emitted as ``None``. A series with no sample in range
492	        is still listed, with an empty ``points`` list, unless ``agg`` is used
493	        without ``step_ms`` (then it yields nothing and is omitted).
494	
495	        ``group_by=None`` keeps this per-series behaviour. Otherwise it must
496	        be a list of distinct non-empty label keys (``[]`` merges every match
497	        into one group) and ``agg`` is required: the raw in-range samples of
498	        all series in a group are aggregated together and each result row
499	        carries only ``labels`` (the group keys present on those series) and
500	        ``points``.
501	
502	        With ``window_ms`` the query switches to sliding-window mode: it
503	        requires ``start_ms``, ``end_ms``, ``step_ms`` and ``agg``, all integer
504	        milliseconds (step and window strictly positive). Evaluation times are
505	        ``start_ms + k*step_ms`` not exceeding ``end_ms``; the point timestamp
506	        is the evaluation time and its value aggregates the raw samples in
507	        ``(t - window_ms, t]`` (left edge excluded, right edge included). The
508	        first window reads history before ``start_ms``, but never anything past
509	        ``t``. Empty windows, including ``count``, emit ``None``. Every matching
510	        series (or group) gets the full time grid even when every window is
511	        empty; no matching series yields an empty list.
512	        """
513	        # Compile before anything else so all matchers are validated even when
514	        # another argument (or the absence of candidate series) would yield an
515	        # empty result.
516	        compiled_matchers = compile_matchers(matchers)
517	        if agg is not None and agg not in AGGREGATES:
518	            raise ObsError("unknown aggregation: %r" % (agg,))
519	        if window_ms is not None:
520	            lo, hi, step, window = self._window_params(
521	                start_ms, end_ms, step_ms, window_ms, agg)
522	            return self._query_windows(tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi, step,
523	                                       agg, group_by, window, compiled_matchers)
524	        if step_ms is not None and (not _num(step_ms) or int(step_ms) <= 0):
525	            raise ObsError("step_ms must be a positive number")
526	        lo = None if start_ms is None else int(start_ms)
527	        hi = None if end_ms is None else int(end_ms)
528	        if lo is not None and hi is not None and hi < lo:
529	            raise ObsError("end_ms must be >= start_ms")
530	        if group_by is not None:
531	            return self._query_grouped(tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi,
532	                                       step_ms, agg, group_by, compiled_matchers)
533	        out = []
534	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels,
535	                                              compiled_matchers):
536	            rows = [item for item in samples
537	                    if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo) and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi)]
538	            points = self._bucket(rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi)
539	            if points is None or (not points and agg is not None and step_ms is None):
540	                continue
541	            out.append({"series_id": sid, "labels": dict(self._series[sid]["labels"]),
542	                        "points": points})
543	        return out
544	
545	    @staticmethod
546	    def _window_params(start_ms, end_ms, step_ms, window_ms, agg):
547	        """Validate sliding-window arguments; return ``(start, end, step, window)``."""
548	        if not isinstance(window_ms, int) or isinstance(window_ms, bool) or window_ms <= 0:
549	            raise ObsError("window_ms must be a positive integer")
550	        if not isinstance(start_ms, int) or isinstance(start_ms, bool):
551	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires an integer start_ms")
552	        if not isinstance(end_ms, int) or isinstance(end_ms, bool):
553	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires an integer end_ms")
554	        if not isinstance(step_ms, int) or isinstance(step_ms, bool) or step_ms <= 0:
555	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires a positive integer step_ms")
556	        if end_ms < start_ms:
557	            raise ObsError("end_ms must be >= start_ms")
558	        if agg is None:
559	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires agg")
560	        return start_ms, end_ms, step_ms, window_ms
561	
562	    def _window_grid(self, start_ms, end_ms, step_ms):
563	        """The ``start_ms + k*step_ms`` evaluation times not past ``end_ms``."""
564	        return range(start_ms, end_ms + 1, step_ms)
565	
566	    def _window_values(self, rows, window, times, agg):
567	        """Aggregate the samples of ``(t - window, t]`` for each ``t``.
568	
569	        ``rows`` is a timestamp-sorted sample list shared by every time. A
570	        sample at the evaluation time is included; one exactly one window
571	        length earlier is excluded. Empty windows (no samples, regardless of
572	        the aggregation, even ``count``) become ``None``.
573	        """
574	        points = []
575	        index = 0
576	        for t in times:
577	            left = t - window
578	            while index < len(rows) and rows[index][0] <= left:
579	                index += 1
580	            values = []
581	            for cursor in range(index, len(rows)):
582	                stamp = rows[cursor][0]
583	                if stamp > t:
584	                    break
585	                values.append(rows[cursor][1])
586	            points.append([t, None if not values else _aggregate(values, agg)])
587	        return points
588	
589	    def _query_windows(self, tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi, step_ms, agg,
590	                       group_by, window, compiled_matchers=()):
591	        if group_by is not None:
592	            if not isinstance(group_by, (list, tuple)):
593	                raise ObsError("group_by must be a list of label keys")
594	            keys = list(group_by)
595	            for key in keys:
596	                if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
597	                    raise ObsError("group_by entries must be non-empty strings")
598	            if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
599	                raise ObsError("group_by entries must not contain duplicates")
600	        times = list(self._window_grid(lo, hi, step_ms))
601	        matched = self._matching_series(tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers)
602	        if group_by is None:
603	            out = []
604	            for sid, series_labels, samples in matched:
605	                points = self._window_values(samples, window, times, agg)
606	                out.append({"series_id": sid, "labels": dict(series_labels),
607	                            "points": points})
608	            return out
609	        groups = {}
610	        for sid, series_labels, samples in matched:
611	            group_labels = {key: series_labels[key] for key in keys
612	                            if key in series_labels}
613	            token = tuple(sorted(group_labels.items()))
614	            entry = groups.setdefault(token, {"labels": group_labels, "rows": []})
615	            # The first window reads history before start_ms; no window reads
616	            # anything past its own evaluation time, so no upper filter applies.
617	            entry["rows"].extend(samples)
618	        out = []
619	        for token in sorted(groups):
620	            entry = groups[token]
621	            rows = sorted(entry["rows"])
622	            out.append({"labels": entry["labels"],
623	                        "points": self._window_values(rows, window, times, agg)})
624	        return out
625	
626	    def _bucket(self, rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi):
627	        """``None`` = nothing to report, ``[]`` = known empty, else the points."""
628	        if step_ms is None:
629	            if agg is None:
630	                return [[stamp, value] for stamp, value in rows]
631	            return None if not rows else [[rows[0][0], _aggregate([v for _, v in rows], agg)]]
632	        step = int(step_ms)
633	        groups = {}
634	        for stamp, value in rows:
635	            groups.setdefault(stamp - (stamp % step), []).append(value)
636	        if not groups:
637	            return None
638	        keys = sorted(groups)
639	        start = max(keys[0], lo - (lo % step)) if lo is not None else keys[0]
640	        end = min(keys[-1], hi - (hi % step)) if hi is not None else keys[-1]
641	        return [[key, _aggregate(groups[key], agg) if key in groups else None]
642	                for key in range(start, end + 1, step)]
643	
644	    def _query_grouped(self, tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi, step_ms, agg, group_by,
645	                       compiled_matchers=()):
646	        """Cross-series aggregation: one row per distinct ``group_by`` tuple.
647	
648	        The raw in-range samples of every series in a group are pooled before
649	        aggregating (no per-series pre-averaging), so samples from different
650	        series at the same timestamp each count. A group key absent from a
651	        series simply does not appear in that group's labels; a missing key
652	        and an empty-string value therefore land in different groups.
653	        """
654	        if not isinstance(group_by, (list, tuple)):
655	            raise ObsError("group_by must be a list of label keys")
656	        keys = list(group_by)
657	        for key in keys:
658	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
659	                raise ObsError("group_by entries must be non-empty strings")
660	        if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
661	            raise ObsError("group_by entries must not contain duplicates")
662	        if agg is None:
663	            raise ObsError("group_by requires agg")
664	        groups = {}
665	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels,
666	                                              compiled_matchers):
667	            series_labels = dict(self._series[sid]["labels"])
668	            group_labels = {key: series_labels[key] for key in keys
669	                            if key in series_labels}
670	            token = tuple(sorted(group_labels.items()))
671	            entry = groups.setdefault(token, {"labels": group_labels, "rows": []})
672	            entry["rows"].extend(item for item in samples
673	                                 if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo)
674	                                 and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi))
675	        out = []
676	        for token in sorted(groups):
677	            entry = groups[token]
678	            rows = sorted(entry["rows"])
679	            if step_ms is None:
680	                points = [] if not rows else \
681	                    [[rows[0][0], _aggregate([value for _, value in rows], agg)]]
682	            else:
683	                points = self._bucket(rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi) or []
684	            out.append({"labels": entry["labels"], "points": points})
685	        return out
686	
687	    def rollup(self, tenant, metric, labels, window_ms, agg):
688	        """Downsampled series over the whole stored range, ordered by series_id."""
689	        if agg not in AGGREGATES:
690	            raise ObsError("unknown aggregation: %r" % (agg,))
691	        if not _num(window_ms) or int(window_ms) <= 0:
692	            raise ObsError("window_ms must be a positive number")
693	        return [{"series_id": item["series_id"], "labels": item["labels"],
694	                 "points": [point for point in item["points"] if point[1] is not None]}
695	                for item in self.query(tenant, metric, labels=labels,
696	                                       step_ms=int(window_ms), agg=agg)]
697	
698	    # --------------------------------------------------------------- retention
699	    def enforce_retention(self, tenant, cutoff_ms):
700	        """Drop every sample with ``timestamp_ms < cutoff_ms`` for ``tenant``."""
701	        cutoff = int(cutoff_ms)
702	        dropped = affected = 0
703	        with self._lock:
704	            for sid in sorted(self._series):
705	                if self._series[sid]["tenant"] != tenant:
706	                    continue
707	                keep = [item for item in self._samples[sid] if item[0] >= cutoff]
708	                removed = len(self._samples[sid]) - len(keep)
709	                if removed:
710	                    self._samples[sid] = keep
711	                    self._rewrite_points(sid)
712	                    dropped += removed
713	                    affected += 1
714	        return {"dropped": dropped, "series": affected, "cutoff_ms": cutoff}
715	
716	    def stats(self):
717	        with self._lock:
718	            per_tenant = {}
719	            points = 0
720	            for sid, row in self._series.items():
721	                count = len(self._samples[sid])
722	                points += count
723	                entry = per_tenant.setdefault(row["tenant"], {"series": 0, "points": 0})
724	                entry["series"] += 1
725	                entry["points"] += count
726	        return {"series": len(self._series), "points": points, "writes": self._writes,
727	                "tenants": per_tenant}

6	import time
7	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
